The words of Executive Order 11708 are in the present tense, so the revocation was performed by the order itself and was executed and exhausted when the order was signed on 1973-03-23; EO 11248 stayed in force only for the positions enumerated in Section 2. The later supersession of EO 11708 by EO 11768 on 1974-02-20 is not the first end of this clause, because a later supersession does not prove first cessation of a command already performed, and the held text of EO 11768 does not revive EO 11248. The surviving effect (EO 11248 revoked, except for the Section 2 positions) is described in the savings statement.

conflict_resolutions.QUARANTINED_RELATIONSHIP_CONFLICT: The ten quarantined relationships (research/stage15/AUDIT/RELATIONSHIP_CHRONOLOGY_VIOLATIONS.csv, edges 6584-6593) are OFR notes on EOs 11389, 11393, 11409, 11441, 11581, 11587, 11604, 11634, 11676 and 11699, each reading (in paraphrase) that it amends EO 11248 of October 10, 1965, which was revoked by EO 11708 of March 23, 1973. Each of those orders was issued before EO 11708 and amended EO 11248; the parenthetical names EO 11708 as the later reviser of EO 11248, which agrees with EO 11708 Sec. 3. None is an event on EO 11708, none can act on a later order, and the Stage 15 audit suppressed them. The four live leads in the packet are the EO 11715, EO 11727 and EO 11736 amendments and the EO 11768 supersession read here.

research_rationale:
EO 11708 (signed 1973-03-23; 38 FR 7979-7980, Federal Register of March 27, 1973, PDF pages 11-12) was read in full from the held official Federal Register text (registered as ORIGINAL:EO:11708). Identity: the heading names Executive Order 11708, Placing Certain Positions in Levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule, dated March 23, 1973, under section 5317 of title 5. The dossier inventory of 25 clauses (Section 1 with items (1)-(14), Section 2 with items (1)-(8), Section 3) was checked against the numbered text and is confirmed complete. The order has three operative parts: Sec. 1 places fourteen positions in level IV, Sec. 2 continues eight positions in level V, and Sec. 3 revokes EO 11248 except for the Section 2 positions. First and whole-order end: express supersession by EO 11768 of February 20, 1974 (39 FR 6693), Sec. 4, effective on signing, 1974-02-20. Earlier ends of single clauses: items (6) and (7) of Section 1 were deleted by EO 11727 Sec. 4, effective as of 1973-07-01 (Sec. 6); item (8) of Section 2 was deleted by EO 11715 Sec. 2 on 1973-04-24; Section 3 was a self-executing revocation performed on 1973-03-23. Amendments that strike and insert text (EO 11715 items (8), (9), (10); EO 11736 items (2), (4), (14)) are later events and the clauses continue, amended, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments, with the before and after text recorded on each clause. Additions (items (15) to (18) of Section 1 and a new item (8) of Section 2) are amendments of the lead clauses of their sections. The whole-order end is the latest first end, 1974-02-20. Searches: the held-text search of the number 11708 returned the orders above and later orders that recite EO 11708 as amended or superseded (EO 11727 Sec. 4 recitals aside, EO 11768 Sec. 4); the packet's machine searches (current-law:usc one lead, which is the printed text of EO 11727 in a note to 21 U.S.C. 801; current-law:ecfr none; later-events:ofr_catalog five leads) were read with their coverage notes and name no other instrument; the 1989 OFR codification row reads, in substance, that the order was amended by EOs 11715, 11727 and 11736 and superseded by EO 11768. The later orders that were not APP-only are cited by their official Federal Register texts (ACTOR_TEXT:EO:11715, EO:11727, EO:11736, EO:11768); no transcription is relied on for any quoted text.

savings.reason: EO 11768 supersedes EO 11708 as amended without saving any of its placements. Its own Sec. 3 protects the appointment of an incumbent from being terminated or requiring reappointment by reason of EO 11768; appointments are not created by EO 11708, so that is not a residual of the superseded order. Where EO 11768 places the same positions in level IV or V again, the pay level rests on EO 11768 as the successor authority, not on EO 11708 or its amending orders. The revocation of EO 11248 performed by EO 11708 Sec. 3 stays performed (EO 11248 was revoked, except for the Section 2 positions), and the held text of EO 11768 does not revive EO 11248. No other savings, transfer or accrued-right provision is found in the held text of EO 11768.
